decisions.executionNote: Memorize red left, angled stem, and blue right, upright stem. Begin elbow-up approach with both open grippers, staying on respective sides.
Raise and advance each elbow-up arm toward its own block; progressively pitch grippers downward.
Continue smooth inward approaches above the blocks without crossing; finish wrist alignment before descending.
Align downward wrists while approaching the stems. Keep each arm in its own half of the workspace.
Finish top-down alignment above the remembered stem centers; inspect wrist views before final descent.
Descend cautiously, correcting visible lateral offsets and red stem yaw. Grippers remain open.
Fine-align the red stem and lower both open jaws to grasp height. Red yaw correction is visual; verify centering before closing.
Close the centered right gripper on blue. Adjust red a few millimeters from wrist RGB before closing the left gripper.
Close both grippers fully at the visually aligned stems and allow closure to settle before testing retention with a lift.
Lift both blocks to verify retention from RGB. Use separated midline table staging to exchange blocks without crossing the arms.
Both blocks remain fixed in the wrist views during lifting. Move toward separated front/red and rear/blue midline staging sites, without crossing arms.
Replan from the executed prefix with smaller increments. Lower toward separated midline staging positions, maintaining closed grippers and elbow-up continuity.
Set both retained blocks down at distinct midline relay sites. Keep grips closed until table contact height is reached.
Release onto the table at the relay sites and retreat upward/outward. Inspect that both blocks stay on the table before changing hands.
Clear the released blocks upward and outward before exchanging fore-aft approach lanes. Begin symmetric jaw-yaw changes for picking the opposite colors.
Move the empty left arm toward the rear blue relay site and the right toward the front red site, with lateral clearance and continuous elbow-up posture.
Continue the separated fore-aft exchange of empty hands. Align each jaw pair with the opposite block's stem using the equivalent 180-degree grasp orientation.
Approach blue with the left and red with the right at separated midline relay sites. Preserve elbow-up configuration and inspect before final descent.
Descend toward the two relay stems from opposite sides of the midline, with small inward corrections and open jaws. Confirm alignment at low height.
Fine-center the relay grasps with small fore-aft and wrist-tilt adjustments, keeping link6 on its own side of the midline. Lower to grasp height.
Close each hand on the opposite-color stem after final millimeter-scale centering. Both arms remain in separated fore-aft relay lanes.
Lift and separate outward while holding both grippers closed. Verify blue is retained by the left and red by the right before rotating toward the remembered target poses.
Both opposite-color grasps are retained in RGB. Carry outward toward the remembered original sites while rotating each block toward the other block's original orientation.
Increase lateral clearance and continue the opposing yaw adjustments toward the memorized poses. Keep both retained blocks above the table.
Bring blue above the original red site and red above the original blue site. Finish most of the remembered orientation swap before the final controlled descent.
Lower the swapped blocks close to table height while leveling them. Refine the right block's fore-aft position and yaw against its remembered blue target.
Place and release red at the remembered blue pose first, then retreat the right hand to give the left wrist more clearance for accurate blue placement.
Set blue down at the remembered red site and release. Move the empty right arm outward, then inspect both released poses before returning home.
Allow the left gripper to open fully, then clear blue upward and outward. Begin smooth elbow-up return while checking the released blocks against their remembered poses.
Both blocks are released in swapped positions with matching visible orientations. Continue outward homeward return with open jaws and elbow-up continuity.
The unobstructed view shows blue slightly forward of the remembered red location. Return the left hand for a small placement correction while the right continues home.
Reapproach blue at its current stem for a small xy correction without changing its orientation. Ease the empty right hand toward its initial pose.
Regrasp blue for a small rightward and nearward placement correction from head RGB. Complete the right arm's return to its starting pose.
Lift blue clear, then translate it about 8 mm right and 12 mm toward the robot to match the memorized red pose. Keep its yaw nearly unchanged.
Lower blue at the corrected remembered pose and release onto the table. Right arm remains at origin, clear of the objects.
Finish opening, clear blue vertically, and start the left arm's continuous elbow-up return. Both blocks should now remain on the table in swapped poses.
Continue the left arm's smooth outward return while unwinding the wrist toward its initial orientation. Keep the released blocks undisturbed and the right arm parked.
Replan the interrupted return from the current pose with smaller translation and rotation increments. Preserve joint continuity and leave both swapped blocks untouched.
Continue the left arm toward origin with decreasing translation steps and smooth wrist unwinding. Both blocks remain released in the exchanged poses.
Finish returning the left arm to its initial pose with tapered translation and continuous wrist rotation; right arm holds origin and both grippers stay open.
